title: Stability Sprint — Release Gateways & Late-Cycle Huddle
content:
Date: 2026-03-10
Meeting: Stability sprint — late-cycle release gateways huddle (weekly)
Attendees: Asha Patel (owner), Michael Chen, Sofia Alvarez, Jonah Reed, Priya Nambiar, Luis Ortega (observer)
Absent: N/A
Location: Zoom + #release-control-thread-3

Objective:
- Align on gating criteria for the 2026.03.12 release window, verify hotfix readiness, and confirm rollback thresholds. Focus is on minimizing blast radius for model-serving changes (runtime kernels + batching).

Agenda:
1) Quick state: current candidate and blocking PRs
2) Canary plan and metric gates (traffic percentages, SLOs)
3) Hotfix/rollback playbook checklist and owners
4) Capacity and GPU pool considerations for Dedicated customers
5) Open risks / decisions / follow-ups

1) Current state & blockers:
- Release candidate: runtime v2.14.0-rc3 (contains attention kernel micro-optimizations and batching rework).
- Blocking PRs called out: PR#987 (kernel selection refactor) — still in CI flakiness; PR#994 (kv-cache edge-case fix) merged but needs perf verification.
- Known regression: intermittent increase in p95 token latency for sequence length >1024 in synthetic perf runs (seen on tpu-like config in CI). Root cause suspected in kernel fallback path when quantized layers hit alignment edge-case.
- Action: Michael to run targeted CI perf suite with 8 seeds on PR#987 today and post results to Slack. Deadline: EOD 2026-03-10.

2) Canary plan & metric gates (finalized):
- Canary cohort: 1% of production traffic for first 15 minutes, then 5% for 45 minutes, then 20% ramp over 2 hours if gates pass.
- Primary metrics to monitor (gates are fail-fast):
  - Request success rate (5xx+4xx) <= 0.25% increase over baseline (baseline = trailing-7d average)
  - p95 latency increase <= 20% relative to baseline for the same sequence-length distribution
  - Token generation error rate (policy/exceptions) no increase > 0.1%
 - Resource/infra metrics:
  - GPU memory OOM events = 0
  - Autoscale loop errors > 0 considered failure
- Canary automation: rollout is controlled by the release bot; manual abort permitted by any oncall. Jonah to validate automation logic (ensuring the bot checks both app and infra metrics) by 2026-03-11 morning.
- Observability: create a temporary dashboard with per-model, per-region views and alerting thresholds; Sofia owning dashboard build (link will be in linked_artifacts once ready).

3) Hotfix & rollback playbook (condensed):
- Triggers for immediate rollback:
  - Any sustained 5xx > 1% for 5 minutes
  - p95 latency breach > 50% for 3 consecutive windows (5m each)
  - OOMs observed across >1 node class
- Emergency patch path:
  - If rollback triggered, release bot initiates automated traffic shift to previous stable artifact (v2.13.x pinned). Team leads notified via pager.
  - Hotfix owners: Priya (cherry-pick coordinator), Michael (runtime test lead), Jonah (deploy conductor).
  - Post-rollback: hotfix branch created from main@stable, patch, run smoke/perf subset, attempt canary with patch within 60–90 mins if low blast risk.
- Communication protocol: status updates every 15 minutes in #release-control-thread-3 and a summary in the release bridge. Asha to draft the status template.

4) Capacity / Dedicated considerations:
- Dedicated (reserved) customers in eu-west-1 may require manual traffic pinning before canary. Plan: for those accounts, we will not route canary traffic automatically; SRE to coordinate manual acceptance.
- Observation: predicted GPU pool saturation for the 20% ramp if qbatch defaults unchanged. Action: Jonah to provision a short-lived burst buffer (2 extra nodes) for 6 hours of ramp window. Jira ticket RI-4821 created for capacity uptick.

5) Open risks / technical debt / decisions:
- Risk A: Kernel refactor introduces subtle floating-point divergence in quantized execution path. Impact: possible tiny semantic differences in output quality. Decision: acceptable within tolerance if eval suite shows L1-norm diff < configured threshold. Action: Sofia to run eval comparison using baseline prompt set (200 prompts) and report delta by 2026-03-11.
- Risk B: Canary automation currently lacks region-aware fallback when region controllers fail. Mitigation: temporarily disable cross-region fallback; keep local fallbacks only. Action: Michael to raise infra ticket if automation not updated by EOD 03/11.
- Risk C: Observability retention for canary traces (too short). We need 2h retention for traces during rollout. Decision: temporarily increase retention for the canary-dashboard window (finance OK for short-lived bump). Asha to coordinate with finance.

Changelog snapshot for release notes (to be included with release):
- runtime v2.14.0-rc3: kernel selection refactor, batching rework for continuous batching, micro-optimizations for attention; includes KV-cache edge-case fix (PR#994).
- Known issue: p95 regression for seq_len>1024 under specific quantized code paths — gating will catch this; documented in release notes.

Action items (owners + target dates):
- Michael Chen: run perf CI on PR#987 (8 seeds), post results to Slack. Target: 2026-03-10 EOD.
- Sofia Alvarez: eval delta report (200 prompts) for quantized path vs baseline. Target: 2026-03-11 AM.
- Jonah Reed: validate release bot canary checks (app + infra), provision burst buffer for ramp window. Target: validate by 2026-03-11 morning; provision complete by 2026-03-12 06:00 UTC.
- Priya Nambiar: prepare hotfix branch template, coordinate cherry-picks. Target: 2026-03-11 EOD.
- Asha Patel: draft status update template and coordinate temporary trace retention bump with finance. Target: 2026-03-11 EOD.

Parking lot / unresolved questions:
- Do we need to add a synthetic canary traffic generator for long-tail prompt distributions? (Raised by Luis) — tentatively yes, but scope is larger than this release. Follow-up: engineering-ops spike next sprint.
- Are Dedicated customers willing to accept 20% ramp in the absence of manual approval? Need to confirm account holders. Action: Customer success to confirm for top-5 Dedicated accounts.

Quick retro from last night's hotfix rehearsal (5m):
- What went well: automated rollback completed in 4m 30s in drill; communication cadence crisp.
- What went wrong: one runbook hyperlink timed out (Confluence permission issue). Quick fix: change runbook share settings and add mirror link to release notes.

Next meeting: 2026-03-11 09:30 UTC (same channel). Goal: final go/no-go signoff and confirmation that PR#987 CI artifacts are green.

Notes captured by: Asha Patel
Document state: working notes (intended to be merged into the release bridge checklist after signoff).

References (quick):
- RI-4821 (capacity upsizing): https://jira.redwood/browse/RI-4821
- Runtime PR#987: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987
- Release gating checklist (confluence): confluence:release-gateways-checklist-2026

---
Small, informal TODOs (personal):
- Asha: confirm that the canary dashboard includes both token-level and request-level alerts (quick check).
- Michael: add stability-run tags to PRs so we can filter test runs faster.

(End of notes)
